title: Leonida Map Size: Comparing Vice City to Los Santos & RDR2
excerpt: Rockstar says Leonida is twice GTA 5 and three times RDR2. But what does that actually mean in square kilometers? Every confirmed claim and the math behind them.
seo_title: GTA 6 Map Size: How Leonida Compares to Los Santos & RDR2
seo_description: GTA 6's Leonida map is projected at 2.3x the size of GTA V's Los Santos. See how Vice City stacks up against Los Santos and RDR2, backed by real data.
content:
How big is the GTA 6 map? It's the question every fan asks, and Rockstar's answer has been characteristically precise about being imprecise.

No official square-kilometer figure exists. What we have instead is better: specific comparisons from Rockstar's own senior developers, reported in [Game Informer](https://www.gameinformer.com) and relayed through creator previews. Let's lay out every number, who said it, and what the math actually means.

## What Rockstar actually said

Two developers, two key statements.

**Aaron Garbut**, Rockstar's art co-president, told Game Informer (September 2026 issue) that Leonida is roughly **twice the size of the GTA 5 map**. He didn't give a kilometer figure. He also called it the biggest map Rockstar has ever built "by some degree" — which includes Red Dead Redemption 2.

**Rob Nelson** of Rockstar North went further in creator preview comments: the map is **twice the size of GTA 5 and three times the playable area of RDR2**. Then he broke it down: **Vice City alone is about twice GTA 5's Los Santos**, and the developed areas outside the city are roughly **11 times the developed space outside Los Santos**.

Those are the confirmed claims. Everything below is arithmetic based on them.

## The math: what "twice GTA 5" means in kilometers

GTA 5's map is generally measured at **75-80 square kilometers** including water, with roughly **48-50 square kilometers** of land.

Double the total: **~150-160 sq km**. Double the land: **~96-100 sq km**.

Here's the catch Nelson's statement doesn't resolve: did he mean total area or land only? Both calculations circulate, and neither is confirmed as what he meant. The honest range is somewhere between 100 and 160 square kilometers depending on how you count water.

## The community measurement: 125 sq km of land

The GTA VI mapping community — the folks doing frame-by-frame trailer reconstruction — has its own number. The mapping project led by GTA Forums user lxr estimates roughly **125 square kilometers of land** for Leonida. By their math, that's about **2.5 times the landmass of GTA 5**.

That's a fan measurement, not an official figure. But it's built on trailer landmarks, Florida geography matching, and a genuinely obsessive methodology. Take it as the best unofficial estimate available.

## GTA 6 vs GTA 5 vs RDR2: the full comparison

| | GTA 5 | RDR2 | GTA 6 (Leonida) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total area | ~75-80 sq km | ~75-85 sq km | ~150-160 sq km (est.) |
| Land area | ~48-50 sq km | ~75 sq km (est.) | ~96-125 sq km (est.) |
| Urban core | Los Santos | Saint Denis | Vice City (~2x Los Santos) |
| Regions | City + desert + mountains | 5 states | 6 distinct regions |
| Setting | Southern California | American frontier | Florida |

The RDR2 comparison deserves a note. RDR2's map was only slightly bigger than GTA 5's — the games are in the same ballpark. So when Nelson says Leonida is three times RDR2's playable area, that's a massive jump. It's the single most aggressive scale claim Rockstar has ever made.


| Game | Map Size (approx.) | Setting |
|------|-------------------|---------|
| GTA 6 (Leonida) | ~125 sq km land | Florida-inspired state |
| GTA 5 (San Andreas) | ~75 sq km | Southern California-inspired |
| Red Dead Redemption 2 | ~75 sq km | American frontier |

## Why raw size isn't the point

Here's what Garbut actually emphasized in the Game Informer piece, and it's more interesting than any kilometer count:

"This new world is different. We obsessed about every part — the rooftops, the alleys, the internals and everything in between to the point we hit a critical mass with the numbers of our interiors, and you start to feel the buildings are more real inside and out."

Translation: Rockstar isn't just making a bigger map. They're making a denser one. More enterable interiors than any previous GTA. Buildings that feel real inside and out. That's the "critical mass" quote, and it's the one that matters.

The six regions tell the same story. Vice City (urban core, 2x Los Santos). Leonida Keys (island chain). Grassrivers (wetlands). Port Gellhorn (faded port town). Ambrosia (industrial). Mount Kalaga (wilderness). That's not just "bigger" — it's six different games' worth of geography stitched together.

## What the trailers show about scale

![Leonida map showing the full GTA 6 game world](/img/leonida-map-v2.jpg)

![Satellite view of Leonida terrain](/img/satellite-map-hd.jpg)

You can feel the size in the footage. Trailer 1's Vice Beach montage shows a dense urban beachfront. Trailer 2 pulls back to wetlands, keys, and farmland. The Extended Look showed transit systems — buses, trains, light rail, taxis, and the RydeMe ride-hailing app — because in a map this size, you need ways to get around that aren't just driving.

There's no universal fast travel. That design choice only makes sense if the map is big enough to make travel itself part of the experience.


## Sources

- [Rockstar Games — Grand Theft Auto VI](https://www.rockstargames.com/VI)
- [Rockstar Games Newswire](https://www.rockstargames.com/newswire)
- [IGN — Grand Theft Auto VI](https://www.ign.com/games/grand-theft-auto-vi)


For a detailed breakdown of each region, see our [GTA 6 Map Guide](/news/gta-6-map-guide-leonida-regions-size). The map's vehicle variety is covered in our [Confirmed Vehicle List](/news/confirmed-vehicle-list-leonida).

## The bottom line

The confirmed facts: twice GTA 5 (Garbut), three times RDR2's playable area (Nelson), Vice City alone twice Los Santos, 11x the developed space outside the city. The estimates: 100-160 sq km depending on methodology.

But the number I'd actually pay attention to isn't a kilometer count. It's Garbut's "critical mass" — the point where interiors, alleys, and rooftops hit a density that makes the world feel real. That's not measurable in square kilometers. And it's the thing that'll determine whether Leonida feels twice as big or ten times as alive.

**Sources:** Aaron Garbut via Game Informer (Sept 2026), Rob Nelson via creator preview (Aug 2026), community mapping by GTA Forums user lxr. All kilometer figures are estimates derived from these claims, not official Rockstar dimensions.

title: GTA 6 Launch Trailer Breakdown
excerpt: Ninety seconds is enough for Rockstar to sharpen the story around GTA 6 without explaining everything. Jason talks about an Army career that ended badly. Lucia reaches him through an automated prison call.
seo_title: GTA 6 Launch Trailer Breakdown: Jason, Lucia & Key Details
seo_description: A scene-by-scene GTA 6 launch trailer breakdown covering Jason's Army past, Lucia's prison call, the Leonida conspiracy and details Rockstar leaves open.
content:
Ninety seconds is enough for Rockstar to sharpen the story around GTA 6 without explaining everything. The launch trailer moves quickly, but it gives Jason and Lucia more character detail than spectacle alone would suggest. Jason talks about an Army career that ended badly. Lucia reaches him through an automated prison call. A supposedly easy score unravels, and the pair are pulled deeper into trouble across Leonida.

The important part is what the trailer actually shows, not the theories around it. Read closely and there is a clear pattern: Jason is running out of clean options, Lucia is still dealing with the consequences of prison, and their relationship sits at the center of whatever goes wrong next.


| Trailer Element | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| Duration | ~90 seconds |
| Focus | Jason's Army past, Lucia's prison call |
| Setting | Leonida (Vice City, Keys, Everglades) |
| Tone | Cinematic, story-driven |

## GTA 6 [Launch Trailer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rz1B4B2yBZY: The Main Takeaways

| Trailer detail | What it tells us |
|---|---|
| Opening location | The trailer begins around the Leonida Keys, grounding Jason in the coastal world tied to his current life. |
| Jason's Army past | Jason says he got into trouble while serving and did not leave the Army on good terms. |
| Lucia's call | Jason receives an automated free call from Lucia, strongly linking this scene to her time in prison. |
| The job goes wrong | A criminal score appears to spiral into a much larger problem involving Jason and Lucia. |
| Major action beats | The trailer shows robberies, gunfire, a helicopter hauling part of a vault, aircraft stunts and police pressure. |
| Relationship focus | Quiet exchanges between Jason and Lucia give the trailer its emotional core. |
| Music | The trailer uses Justice's "Flower in a Hurricane" as a major part of its pace and tone. |

## What Actually Happens in the GTA 6 Launch Trailer?

The trailer opens above the Leonida Keys, with blue water, marinas and a sun-baked coastal atmosphere doing most of the establishing work. It is a calmer start than the chaos that follows, and it places Jason back in the part of Leonida that has become closely associated with him.

![Florida Keys Marina - GTA 6 Launch Trailer Opening Shot](/img/trailer-keys-marina.webp)

From there, the trailer cuts between character moments and increasingly elaborate crime scenes. Jason talks about his past. His phone lights up with an automated call from Lucia. We then get robberies, armed confrontations, a helicopter lifting away part of a bank vault, a plane-related stunt and brief flashes of the pair together while everything around them becomes less controlled.

The sequence is not built like a mechanics showcase. There is no visible HUD, no tutorial-style explanation and no attempt to walk through systems one by one. The editing is doing something simpler: showing how fast an ordinary criminal job can turn into a problem neither Jason nor Lucia can handle alone.

## Jason's Army Past Gets Its Clearest Explanation Yet

The most useful character detail comes from Jason himself. He says he got into trouble in the Army and did not leave on good terms. That is specific enough to change how his situation reads, but still vague enough that the trailer leaves the real story untouched.

What happened? The trailer does not say. It does not identify the incident, the consequences or the exact terms of his departure. That matters because it keeps the evidence separate from speculation. What we can say is that Jason sees his past as something that still limits him. He talks like a man who believes conventional routes, loans, second chances and easy exits are no longer available to him.

![Jason Duval at Brian's Marina - GTA 6 Launch Trailer](/img/trailer-jason-marina.webp)

That gives his criminal life more weight. He is not presented as someone chasing danger simply because he enjoys it. The trailer frames him as someone who has already burned through safer options and knows it. You can dig into the full cast on our [characters page](/characters).

## Why Lucia's Prison Call Matters

Lucia gets one of the trailer's most revealing moments without appearing in a large action scene. Jason answers his phone and an automated message announces a free call from Lucia. The obvious implication is that she is calling while still incarcerated.

The trailer does not provide a timestamp or a complete chronology, so it would be too strong to claim exactly where the call sits in the story. But it does establish something important: Jason and Lucia are already connected while prison is still part of Lucia's life.

![Lucia Caminos Prison Call - GTA 6 Launch Trailer](/img/trailer-lucia-call.webp)

Later shots show Lucia wearing an ankle monitor. The device clearly signals some form of legal restriction after custody, but the trailer does not define the condition. Calling it probation, parole or house arrest would go beyond what is actually shown.

Those details make Lucia's freedom feel conditional. She may be out, but the trailer keeps reminding us that prison and its consequences have not simply disappeared from her story.

## Jason and Lucia Are the Real Center of the Trailer

For all the money, weapons and vehicles on screen, the trailer keeps returning to the two leads. Lucia quietly asks whether they are going to be okay. Jason answers from a place of shared history, essentially arguing that they have made it through everything else together and only need to survive what comes next.

That exchange is more important than most of the explosions. The trailer is not selling two separate protagonists who happen to share missions. It is selling a partnership under pressure. Their trust, fear and dependence on each other are treated as part of the stakes.

The kiss shown against the surrounding gunfire pushes the same idea visually. GTA 6 may be full of criminal spectacle, but this trailer makes the relationship the thing holding that spectacle together.

## The "Easy Score" Clearly Does Not Stay Easy

The trailer repeatedly contrasts confidence with consequences. Jobs begin with the familiar GTA language of cash, vehicles and quick plans, then escalate into heavier police pressure and much larger set pieces.

The helicopter sequence is the clearest example. Watching part of a bank vault being hauled through the air immediately tells you this is not a small robbery anymore. The scale has changed. The same is true of the aircraft stunt and the number of armed confrontations packed into such a short trailer.

![Helicopter Hauling Bank Vault - GTA 6 Launch Trailer Heist](/img/trailer-vault-heli.webp)

What the trailer does not explain is just as important. It does not identify who sits behind the wider conspiracy, which job triggers it, or why Jason and Lucia become central to it. That information is deliberately withheld. The launch trailer gives us the shape of the problem without giving away the machinery behind it.

## The Trailer Uses Leonida as More Than a Backdrop

Even in a fast edit, the trailer keeps changing the kind of space around Jason and Lucia. The Keys feel open and sun-bleached. Marinas and roads give way to denser crime scenes, interiors and high-speed movement. That variation helps the trailer sell the idea that their trouble is not confined to one corner of the map.

The important detail is not simply that Leonida looks large. It is that the trailer makes movement across the state feel tied to the story. Jason and Lucia are not sightseeing. Each new location appears to be another stage in a situation that keeps widening around them. Explore the full state on our [Leonida map](/map).

## What the Justice Track Adds to the Trailer

The music does more than sit behind the footage. Justice's "Flower in a Hurricane" gives the trailer a restless, almost euphoric momentum that clashes with how badly things appear to be going for the characters.

That contrast works. The images keep getting more dangerous while the track keeps pushing forward. Instead of turning the trailer into a grim crime montage, the music preserves the heat, color and reckless confidence that GTA marketing usually thrives on.

It also gives the quieter Jason and Lucia scenes room to land. The result feels less like a list of features and more like a compressed story beat with a beginning, escalation and emotional payoff.

### What the GTA 6 Launch Trailer Still Doesn't Tell Us

The trailer answers enough to make Jason and Lucia clearer, but it deliberately leaves the central mysteries open.

It does not explain what Jason did in the Army or exactly how his service ended.

It does not establish the precise timeline of Lucia's prison call.

It does not define the legal terms behind Lucia's ankle monitor.

It does not identify the job that turns into the larger conspiracy.

It does not reveal who is behind that conspiracy or what they want from Jason and Lucia.

It does not explain which action scenes belong to the same mission and which come from different parts of the story.

That restraint is what makes the trailer effective. It gives the audience concrete character information while protecting the larger plot. You come away knowing more about Jason and Lucia, but not enough to map the entire story before playing it. For a refresher on the previous big story drop, check out our [Trailer 2 breakdown](/news/gta-6-trailer-2-breakdown).

### The Biggest Takeaway From the Trailer

The GTA 6 launch trailer is at its best when it stops being about the size of the robberies and focuses on why Jason and Lucia keep choosing each other.

Jason enters the story carrying a military past he clearly regrets. Lucia's prison call and ankle monitor show that incarceration still shapes her situation. Their criminal plans keep growing more dangerous, yet the trailer repeatedly cuts back to private conversations and shared uncertainty.

That is the clearest message in the full 90 seconds: the real pressure point in GTA 6 is not whether Jason and Lucia can pull off another score. It is whether their partnership survives once that score turns into something much bigger than either of them expected.

## GTA 6 Launch Trailer FAQ

### What does Jason reveal about his Army past?

Jason says he got into trouble in the Army and did not leave on good terms. The trailer does not explain the incident or the exact circumstances of his departure.

### Is Lucia still in prison during the phone call?

The automated message strongly suggests Lucia is calling Jason from custody. The trailer does not provide a precise timeline, so the exact placement of the scene remains unconfirmed.

### What does Lucia's ankle monitor mean?

It shows that Lucia is under some form of legal restriction, but the trailer does not specify whether that means probation, parole, house arrest or another condition.

### What major action scenes appear in the trailer?

The footage includes robberies, gunfights, a helicopter carrying part of a bank vault, an aircraft stunt, police pressure and several fast-cut criminal set pieces.

### What is the main story clue in the trailer?

The strongest clue is that an apparently straightforward score goes wrong and pulls Jason and Lucia into a much larger criminal problem across Leonida.

### What song is used in the GTA 6 launch trailer?

The trailer features Justice's "Flower in a Hurricane," which drives much of its pacing and atmosphere.

- [Rockstar Games — Grand Theft Auto VI](https://www.rockstargames.com/VI)
- [Rockstar Games Newswire](https://www.rockstargames.com/newswire)

title: GTA 6 Map Guide: Leonida Regions, Size & Locations
excerpt: GTA 6 takes place in Leonida — Rockstar's Florida — with six distinct regions and a Vice City twice the size of Los Santos. Here's every confirmed location and what we know about the map.
seo_title: GTA 6 Map: Leonida Regions, Size & All Locations Guide
seo_description: Explore the GTA 6 map: all 6 Leonida regions, Vice City size vs GTA 5, travel systems, and every confirmed location. The complete Leonida geography guide.
content:
## Where Is GTA 6 Set?

Leonida. The fictional state of Leonida — [Rockstar](https://www.rockstargames.com/VI's take on Florida — with a rebuilt, modern-day Vice City at its center. It's the series' first return to Vice City since GTA: Vice City Stories back in 2006, which is honestly staggering to think about. The map spans six confirmed regions, running from tropical keys to swamplands to mountain parks.

All of this is confirmed: the Leonida setting, the six region names, Vice City as the centerpiece. The size figures further down are a different story — those are reported and estimated, and we'll be clear about which is which.

## How Big Is the GTA 6 Map?

Rockstar hasn't published official dimensions. What we have are scale claims from two senior developers in interviews. Aaron Garbut, Rockstar's art co-president, says Leonida is roughly twice the size of the GTA 5 map. Rob Nelson at Rockstar North goes further: Vice City alone is about 2x GTA 5's Los Santos, and the developed areas outside the city are roughly 11x the developed space outside Los Santos.

Fans and outlets have done the arithmetic and landed on around 160 square kilometers for Leonida, versus about 80 for GTA 5 and 75 for Red Dead Redemption 2. But treat every square-kilometer figure as an estimate, not confirmed data. There is no official number.

Honestly, raw size matters less than density here. Rockstar keeps emphasizing more enterable interiors than any previous GTA, plus deliberately unmarked discoveries — no objectives, no blips, no icons — that reward just wandering around. It's very much in the RDR2 spirit, and that's the part that has us most excited.


| Region | Key Features |
|--------|-------------|
| Vice City | Main city, beaches, nightlife |
| Leonida Keys | Island chain, marinas, smuggling routes |
| Port Gellhorn | Industrial port area |
| Ambrosia | Rural, industrial |
| Mount Kalaga | Mountainous, wilderness |
| Grassrivers | Wetlands, Everglades-inspired |

## The Six Regions of Leonida

![Leonida map showing all six regions](/img/leonida-map-v2.jpg)

### 1. Vice City

The Miami-inspired urban core and the game's centerpiece. Neon-soaked beachfront, downtown skylines, nightlife districts, and the criminal heart of Leonida. Per Nelson, Vice City alone is roughly twice the size of GTA 5's Los Santos — let that sink in.

**Seen in:** Both trailers, the Netflix Extended Look.

### 2. Leonida Keys

A tropical archipelago — Florida Keys by way of Rockstar — with islands stitched together by bridges. Jason grew up here among small-time grifters, and Brian Heder's smuggling operation is based here. Boats, seaplanes, island-hopping. Expect the Keys to be where the game's maritime side really shines.

**Seen in:** Trailer 2 (Jason's backstory).

### 3. Grassrivers

Everglades-style swamps and wetlands — airboats, alligators, remote hideouts. If you remember the alligator-in-a-convenience-store shot from Trailer 1, that's pure Grassrivers energy.

**Seen in:** Trailer 1, Trailer 2.

### 4. Port Gellhorn

A faded west-coast tourist and dock town — crime-infested, weathered, past its prime. Docks, warehouses, and the kind of place where deals go wrong. This one carries some real Vice City 2002 energy, and we mean that as a compliment.

### 5. Ambrosia

The industrial center beside Lake Leonida — factories, breweries, sugar-farming towns. Blue-collar Leonida, about as far from the Vice City glitz as you can get.

**Seen in:** Trailer 2.

### 6. Mount Kalaga National Park

Forests, rivers, and mountains on Leonida's northern border — confirmed for off-road racing, and home to some affluent neighborhoods. The wilderness playground.

**Seen in:** Trailer 2.

## Map Features & Travel

![Satellite view of Leonida](/img/satellite-map-hd.jpg)

### No Universal Fast Travel

There's no magic fast-travel button, so get comfortable with Leonida's transit options:

- **Buses, trains, and light rail**
- **Taxis**
- **"RydeMe"** (ride-hailing app, Uber parody) — you can **skip the ride** or **chat with NPC passengers** along the way

We already have opinions about which NPCs we're going to get trapped with.

### Exploration Philosophy

Rockstar wants you to actually explore, and the map is designed around that idea. The full map opens shortly after the intro rather than being gated by story progress. The pause-menu map has a satellite style. Unmarked discoveries carry no objectives, blips, or icons — exploring is rewarded for its own sake. And cityscapes change as the story progresses, which is a quietly huge feature. The Leonida you start in won't be the one you finish in.

### Interiors

Rockstar promises more enterable interiors than any previous GTA — a direct answer to one of the fandom's longest-running requests. After years of beautiful but sealed storefronts, this is the one that has us smiling.

## Confirmed Locations Within Regions

- **Vice Beach** — the iconic oceanfront (Trailer 1)
- **Leonida Penitentiary** — where Lucia's story begins
- **Ocean Beach** — home to the pre-order bonus garage
- **Mega Mundo** — site of the Extended Look security mission
- **Lake Leonida** — beside Ambrosia's industrial zone
- **Only Raw Records** — Boobie Ike's music label HQ

Track every location on our interactive [GTA 6 map](/map).


Compare map sizes in our [Leonida Map Size vs GTA 5 & RDR2](/news/map-size-comparison-gtav-rdr2). See every vehicle in our [Confirmed Vehicle List](/news/confirmed-vehicle-list-leonida).

## GTA 6 Map vs GTA 5 Map

| | GTA 5 (Los Santos & Blaine County) | GTA 6 (Leonida) |
|---|---|---|
| Setting | Southern California | Florida |
| Urban core | Los Santos | Vice City (~2x Los Santos per Nelson) |
| Total scale | Baseline (~80 sq km est.) | ~2x GTA 5 (per Garbut) |
| Regions | City + desert + mountains | 6 distinct regions |
| Interiors | Limited | Most in series history |
| Fast travel | Taxis only | Transit + RydeMe app |

One important note: every size comparison here comes from developer interview claims and outlet estimates — not official Rockstar dimensions. Read all of them as approximations.


## Sources

- [Rockstar Games — Grand Theft Auto VI](https://www.rockstargames.com/VI)
- [GTA 6 Trailer 1 (YouTube)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QdBZY2fkU-0)
- [GTA 6 Trailer 2 (YouTube)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FKUW7_I4QwA)

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Where is GTA 6 set?
The fictional state of Leonida — Rockstar's Florida — with a modern-day Vice City at its heart.

### How big is the GTA 6 map?
Roughly twice the size of GTA 5's map, per Rockstar's Aaron Garbut. But that's a reported figure — no official dimensions exist.

### What are the GTA 6 map regions?
Six of them, all confirmed: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga National Park.

### Is Vice City bigger than Los Santos?
Per Rockstar North's Rob Nelson, yes — Vice City alone is roughly twice GTA 5's Los Santos.

### Does GTA 6 have fast travel?
No universal fast travel. Instead you've got buses, trains, light rail, taxis, and the RydeMe ride-hailing app.

### When does the full GTA 6 map unlock?
Shortly after the intro, from what Rockstar has said. The map isn't gated by story progress.

title: Port Gellhorn in GTA 6: Locations, Story Clues and What Rockstar Confirmed
excerpt: Port Gellhorn is Rockstar's 'forgotten coast': cheap motels, empty strip malls and a rough new economy. This guide separates official details, visible trailer locations and unconfirmed map theories.
seo_title: Port Gellhorn GTA 6 Guide: Locations and Story Clues
seo_description: Port Gellhorn is GTA 6's faded coastal town in Leonida. See its confirmed locations, story clues, atmosphere and what Rockstar has not revealed yet.
content:
**Quick answer:** Port Gellhorn is a confirmed GTA 6 region in Leonida. Rockstar describes it as a once-popular coastal vacation spot left with cheap motels, closed attractions and empty strip malls. Official imagery shows a motel, a grow-room scene, a package handoff, a cabaret parking lot and other signs of an underground economy.

## What is Port Gellhorn in GTA 6?

Port Gellhorn is one of the major Leonida locations Rockstar introduced alongside Trailer 2. Its identity is deliberately different from Vice City's neon glamour. Rockstar frames it as a coastal resort town that lost its tourist economy and never fully recovered.

The official description focuses on cheap motels, shut-down attractions and empty strip malls, then replaces tourism with a rougher economy built around alcohol, painkillers and truck-stop culture. That language matters because it tells us what the area is for: Port Gellhorn is meant to feel worn down, local and economically improvised.

Port Gellhorn also matters because its smaller crimes and rougher economy contrast with the larger jobs Jason and Lucia take on later. See the [GTA 6 missions hub](https://www.taishgaming.com/missions) for the gameplay side of that escalation.

## Where is Port Gellhorn on the GTA 6 map?

Rockstar has confirmed Port Gellhorn as a Leonida destination, but it has not published a complete official GTA 6 map with a precise border, county assignment or coordinate system.

That distinction is important. Community mapping projects can be useful for orientation, but they are reconstructions built from trailers, screenshots and, in some cases, material that Rockstar has not officially published. Those projects should not be written as if Rockstar has confirmed their exact geography.

Port Gellhorn is a confirmed Leonida coastal region, but its exact official position and boundaries remain unreleased.

## Which Port Gellhorn locations have been shown?

Several businesses and visual landmarks are associated with Port Gellhorn through official footage, official screenshots and readable signage. The strongest examples include Uncle Jack's Liquor, Port Gellhorn Pawn & Gun, the Starlet Motel and Delights Cabaret.

Rockstar's own Port Gellhorn imagery also shows a motel at night, an indoor grow-room scene, a woman handing a package into a car, a cabaret parking area and a bonfire gathering. These details reinforce the region's identity even when Rockstar does not give every building a formal name.

What should not be assumed is equally important. A visible doorway does not automatically prove a shop is freely enterable. A story scene near a business does not confirm repeatable robberies. A screenshot does not prove a property can be purchased.

## Does Port Gellhorn appear in Jason and Lucia's crime story?

The trailers repeatedly associate the Port Gellhorn look with lower-level crime: liquor-store imagery, a pawn-and-gun business, cheap accommodation and informal exchanges. That makes the region a natural fit for the couple's early criminal life.

However, Rockstar's official story synopsis does not say that Port Gellhorn is the opening area, and it does not identify the location of the 'easy score' that goes wrong. Treating Port Gellhorn as the confirmed starting hub would go beyond the evidence.

Port Gellhorn therefore represents the small-scale, rough-edged side of Leonida, in sharp contrast with the money, nightlife and spectacle of Vice City.

## Is Port Gellhorn based on a real Florida town?

Rockstar has not named a single real-world model for Port Gellhorn. The phrase 'forgotten coast' naturally invites comparisons with Florida's Gulf and Panhandle communities, and some visible buildings have been matched by fans to real properties.

Those comparisons can be useful as context, but they should remain clearly labeled as community analysis. A location can draw from several Florida places at once, especially in a fictional state built to compress and exaggerate regional culture.

That distinction matters because Port Gellhorn may echo several real Florida communities, but Rockstar has not confirmed a single real-world model for the region.

## What about Gellhorn International Raceway?

The name Gellhorn International Raceway circulates widely in community databases and leak-based references. That is not the same as Rockstar confirming a Port Gellhorn racetrack on its public location page.

The August 2026 Extended Look does show racing activity, but the footage does not by itself prove the track's official name or exact location. Until Rockstar names it directly, the raceway should not be listed as a confirmed Port Gellhorn location.

Until Rockstar names the track directly, it is better treated as an unconfirmed community label rather than an official Port Gellhorn location.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Is Port Gellhorn confirmed in GTA 6?**

Yes. Rockstar lists Port Gellhorn as one of the major destinations in Leonida.

**What is Port Gellhorn like?**

Rockstar describes it as a faded coastal vacation town with cheap motels, closed attractions, empty strip malls and a rough replacement economy.

**Is Port Gellhorn the starting area in GTA 6?**

Not officially. The trailers connect the region with smaller crimes, but Rockstar has not confirmed that the game begins there.

**Where exactly is Port Gellhorn?**

Rockstar has not published a complete official map showing its precise boundaries. Community maps are useful but should not be treated as first-party confirmation.

**Is Gellhorn International Raceway confirmed by Rockstar?**

The name is widely used in community and leak-derived references, but Rockstar has not clearly named it on the official Port Gellhorn location material. Racing is shown, but the official track identity remains unconfirmed.
